title: What's next on the backlog?

criteria.why: `factory.py next mold_v1` prints mold_v1-005: the highest-priority todo task whose dependencies are done

expected_answer: mold_v1-005  Load lane: raise the concurrency target to 50 chats (mold_v1-003 has higher priority but is blocked by mold_v1-006; mold_v1-004 is already in progress)
final_text:
The next task on the mold_v1 backlog is **mold_v1-005: "Load lane: raise the concurrency target to 50 chats"**.

- It's a P2 test task for the `harbor` product, assigned to fable.
- It doesn't depend on any other task, so it can start now.
- It counts as done once the 50-chat target is verified and the evidence is recorded.

The rest of the backlog:

| Task | Priority | Status | What |
|---|---|---|---|
| mold_v1-004 | P1 | **in progress** | Keyboard focus ring on the chat composer |
| mold_v1-003 | P1 | todo, blocked by 006 | Release gate: onboarding path works end to end |
| mold_v1-006 | P2 | todo | Write the operator runbook (brief to live app) |
| mold_v1-008 | P2 | blocked | Workspace export to CSV |
| mold_v1-007 | P3 | todo | Responsiveness lane: add a 320 px viewport |

One alternative: 006 is the only thing blocking the P1 release gate (003). If getting toward release matters more than the load target right now, do the runbook first.

Should I start on 005? That means marking it in progress and then working on the load lane.
